Astra.description:
Astra DevOps / secure-connect-bundle auto-download (`CFG-110`).

**Astra DB only.** Every property in this section is ignored for self-managed Apache
Cassandra, DSE, HCD and ScyllaDB.

custom_domain.description: The custom domain the bundle should be issued for.

database_id.description: The Astra database UUID, used to download a bundle through the DevOps API.

metadata_refresh_interval.description: How often to refresh Astra control-connection metadata (`CON-025`).

mode.description:
How CQL traffic reaches Astra (`CON-022`, `CON-026`).

`sni` follows the bundle's `config.json`; `single_endpoint` is for deployments
that terminate SNI upstream.

region.description: The Astra region whose bundle to download, for multi-region databases.

scb_type.description: Whether to download the standard bundle or a custom-domain one.

AstraDatabaseId.description: The Astra database UUID, as shown in the Astra console.

AstraMode.description: How to route CQL traffic to Astra (`CON-022`, `CON-026`).

oneOf.description: SNI proxy routing, as the bundle's `config.json` describes it.
A single endpoint, for deployments that terminate SNI upstream.

Auth.description: How callers of the HTTP control plane authenticate (`SEC-010`).

AuthMode.description: How the HTTP control plane authenticates callers (`SEC-010`).

oneOf.description: No authentication. Only safe on a loopback bind.
A bearer token in the `Authorization` header.
Mutual TLS.

Autocorrect.description: What the validate job repairs when it finds a difference (`CFG-140`).

mismatch.description: Overwrite target rows whose values differ from origin.

missing.description: Write rows that are present on origin and absent on target.

missing_counter.description:
Write missing rows even for a counter table.

Dangerous: re-inserting a deleted counter row double-counts it. Off by default.

BatchGrouping.description:
How rows are grouped into a write batch (`MIG-022`).

A Cassandra `UNLOGGED` batch that spans partitions is not an optimisation: the coordinator
fans it out to every replica set involved and the batch finishes no sooner than its slowest
participant. The only batch that is faster than the individual writes it replaces is a
single-partition one, which the coordinator applies as a single mutation.

oneOf.description: Rows belonging to different partitions are never batched together.

Java's behaviour: rows are appended in the order they are read, whatever partition they
belong to, and the batch is sent once it reaches `perfops.batch_size`.

enabled.description: Coordinate token ranges with other cdm-rs processes through the tracking table.

heartbeat_interval.description: How often a node renews its leases and refreshes its membership row.

lease_duration.description: How long a range lease is held before another node may reclaim it (`DST-012`).

node_id.description: This node's identity in the membership table.

ratelimit_is_global.description:
Treat `perfops.ratelimit.*` as a budget for the whole cluster (`ENG-004`).

Off, every node applies the configured limit itself, so *n* nodes hit the origin
*n* times as hard — which is usually a surprise. On, each node takes an equal share
of the limit based on the live membership count, so the number that was configured
is the number the clusters actually see.

Only meaningful when `cluster.enabled` is set; a single node's share of a limit is
the whole limit.

ColumnFilter.description: A single-column equality filter applied in cdm-rs (`CFG-180`).

value.description: The value the column must equal, compared as a string.

origin.description: The cluster data is read from.

target.description: The cluster data is written to.

read.description: Consistency level for reads from the origin.

write.description: Consistency level for writes to the target.

ConsistencyLevel.description:
A CQL consistency level (`CFG-160`).

Unlike Java CDM, an unrecognised value is a Tier-1 error rather than a silent coercion to
`LOCAL_QUORUM` (`CFG-161`); `--compat-java` restores the coercion.

oneOf.description: Any node, including a hinted handoff target. Writes only.
One replica.
Two replicas.
Three replicas.
A quorum of all replicas.
One replica in the local datacentre.
A quorum of the local datacentre's replicas. The default.
A quorum in every datacentre.
Linearisable consistency, cluster-wide.
Linearisable consistency within the local datacentre.
Every replica.

ConstantColumns.description: Columns written with a fixed value on every row (`CFG-190`).

names.description: Target columns to populate with a constant.

split_regex.description:
The regular expression that splits
[`values`](ConstantColumns::values), for literals that contain commas.

values.description:
The constants, as CQL literals, in the order of
[`names`](ConstantColumns::names) (`CFG-030`).

oneOf.description: Events are not emitted.
One JSON object per line on standard output.
One JSON object per line in a file.

path.description:
The file the `file` sink appends to (`MET-030`).

Ignored unless [`sink`](Events::sink) is `file`. The sink appends rather than
truncating, so a resumed run (`TRK-031`) adds to the record of the run it resumes
instead of erasing it; point two concurrent runs at one path and their events
interleave in one stream, which is usually what you want and never a corruption,
since NDJSON is line-delimited.

ExplodeMap.description: Turning one origin map into many target rows (`CFG-190`, `CFG-031`).

origin_column.description: The origin map column to explode.

target_key_column.description: The target column that receives each map key.

target_value_column.description: The target column that receives each map value.

ExtractJson.description: Lifting JSON properties out of a text column into target columns (`CFG-190`).

exclusive.description: Migrate only the extracted columns, not the JSON column itself.

origin_column.description: The origin column holding a JSON document.

overwrite.description: Overwrite a target column that already holds a value.

property_mapping.description: The mapping from JSON property to target column, as `property:column` pairs.

constant_columns.description: Columns written with a fixed value on every row.

explode_map.description: Turning one origin map into many target rows.

extract_json.description: Lifting JSON properties out of a text column into target columns.

guardrail.description: Limits that make a row be skipped and reported rather than written.

Filter.description: Which rows take part in the run (`CFG-180`).

column.description: A single-column equality filter applied in cdm-rs, not in CQL.

cql_where.description: A CQL predicate appended to the origin `SELECT`, without the `WHERE` keyword.

token.description: The slice of the token ring to process.

token_coverage_percent.description: Percentage of each token range to process, for sampling runs.

Guardrail.description: Limits that make a row be skipped and reported rather than written (`CFG-190`).

column_size_kb.description:
Report any column whose serialised size exceeds this. `0` disables the check.

A negative value is invalid (`CFG-035`).

mode.description:
What an inline guardrail violation does to the row that caused it (`GRD-004`).

Only consulted when the guardrail runs *inside* a migrate or validate run. The
standalone `cdm guardrail` job always reports and never writes, so the mode cannot
change what it does.

GuardrailMode.description:
What an inline guardrail violation does to the row that caused it (`GRD-004`).

The column-size guardrail reports; it does not filter. So the default changes nothing about
what a run writes: `check` counts the row `LARGE` and carries on, which is the only
behaviour Java has — its guardrail is a job of its own and never runs alongside a migration.
`warn` is the same judgement said more quietly, for a run that wants the finding in the log
without an `ERROR` line per row. `block` is the one mode that changes the outcome: the row
is counted `LARGE` and *not* written, which is what an operator wants when the target
enforces a column-size limit and a migration that skips the handful of rows over it is far
more useful than one that fails on them.

oneOf.description: Count the row `LARGE`, report it at `ERROR`, and process it as normal. Java's behaviour.
As `check`, but the finding is reported at `WARN`.
Count the row `LARGE` and skip it: nothing is written for it (`GRD-004`).

KeyStore.description: The key store of one side (`CFG-120`).

path.description: Path to the key store holding the client certificate.

oneOf.description: Human-readable, multi-line, coloured when the terminal supports it.
One JSON object per record.
Human-readable, one line per record.

diff_file.description: Where the validate job writes its row-level difference log.

OriginColumns.description: Column selection and renaming on the origin side (`CFG-130`).

skip.description: Origin columns to leave out of the run.

OriginSchema.description: The origin side of the schema (`CFG-130`).

keyspace_table.description:
The origin table, as `keyspace.table`.

The only unconditionally required property (`CFG-022`).

ttl.description: Which columns supply the TTL of a migrated row.

writetime.description: Which columns supply the writetime of a migrated row.

endpoint.description: The OTLP collector endpoint. Export is off when unset.

adaptive_ratelimit.description: Reduce the rate limit automatically when the target signals overload.

batch_grouping.description:
How rows are grouped into a write batch (`MIG-022`).

`strict` never puts two partitions in one batch, which is the only batching that
is faster than the writes it replaces. `legacy` reproduces Java's index-order
batching exactly.

batch_size.description:
Rows per write batch.

Coerced to 1 for counter tables and when a writetime filter is active
(`CFG-040`, `MIG-021`).

error_limit.description: Stop the run after this many row-level errors. `0` means never stop.

fetch_size.description: Rows read from the origin per page.

max_inflight_reads.description: Maximum read requests in flight across all workers.

max_inflight_writes.description: Maximum write requests in flight across all workers.

num_parts.description:
Number of token-range splits the ring is divided into.

Rule of thumb: one part per 10 MB of table data.

shutdown_grace.description:
How long a graceful shutdown lets in-flight ranges finish (`ENG-010`).

After a `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` the scheduler stops claiming new ranges and waits
this long for the ones already running. It is a deadline, not a request: a range
that has not finished by then is abandoned and stays unclaimed for a resume, which
is why the value is worth raising on a cluster whose individual ranges are slow.

enabled.description: Serve `/metrics`. Defaults to whether the control plane is enabled.

origin.description: Rows read per second, per cdm-rs process.

target.description: Rows written per second, per cdm-rs process.

initial_backoff.description: Delay before the first retry; doubles each attempt.

max_attempts.description: How many times a failed request is retried before the range fails.

ScbType.description: Which secure-connect-bundle the Astra DevOps API should hand back (`CFG-110`).

oneOf.description: The bundle for the database's primary region.
A bundle for a custom domain.

SchemaSettings.description: Which tables and columns take part in the run (`CFG-130`).

origin.description: The origin table and its column handling.

ttl_writetime.description: How TTL and writetime are calculated.

Secret.description: A credential. Accepts the literal value or the indirection forms `env:VAR`, `file:/path` and `exec:command` (CFG-012).

bind.description:
The address the control plane listens on.

Binding anywhere other than loopback without authentication is refused
(`SEC-010`).

SideConnect.description:
One side's connection (`CFG-100`).

Declared once and instantiated twice; the `{side}` placeholder in each legacy alias is
substituted with `origin` or `target` when the registry is built.

astra.description: Astra DevOps API settings for downloading the bundle (`CFG-110`).

host.description:
Contact point host name or IP address.

This is the normal way to reach Apache Cassandra, DSE, HCD and ScyllaDB. Either
this or [`scb`](SideConnect::scb) must be set for the side, and setting both is an
error (`CFG-024`, `CFG-041`).

local_datacenter.description:
The datacenter the load-balancing policy treats as local (`CON-009`).

Left unset, it is auto-detected from the contact point's `system.local`, which is
right for every single-region deployment. Set it when the process runs in a
different datacenter from the one it should read or write, or when the cluster
spans regions and `LOCAL_QUORUM` must resolve locally.

New in cdm-rs: Java CDM has no equivalent property and always lets the driver
choose (`ConnectionFetcher`, `CDM-31`).

password.description:
Password, or the Astra token.

Supports `env:VAR`, `file:/path` and `exec:command` indirection (`CFG-012`).

scb.description:
Path to an Astra DB secure-connect-bundle zip.

**Astra DB only.** Self-managed Apache Cassandra, DSE, HCD and ScyllaDB use
[`host`](SideConnect::host) and [`port`](SideConnect::port); a cluster with client
encryption uses the `tls` section, which is a separate mechanism and not a bundle.

Set this or [`host`](SideConnect::host) for the side, never both (`CFG-041`). For
Astra you can skip the file entirely and set
[`astra.database_id`](Astra::database_id) instead, which downloads the bundle
through the DevOps API (`CON-004`).

tls.description:
TLS settings for a self-managed cluster with client encryption (`CFG-120`).

This is how you reach an OSS Cassandra, DSE or HCD cluster over TLS — truststore,
keystore and cipher suites. It is unrelated to the Astra secure-connect-bundle.

username.description: Username, or the literal `token` when authenticating to Astra.

Speculative.description:
Speculative execution for one side (`CFG-100`, `CON-010`).

A speculative execution is a second copy of a request, started when the first has not
answered within [`delay`](Speculative::delay) and raced against it. It trades throughput
for tail latency, and it is **off by default** — most of all for the target, where a
second copy of a non-idempotent write is a correctness problem rather than a performance
one. cdm-rs refuses to speculate on a counter table whatever this section says
(`CON-012`).

New in cdm-rs: Java CDM has no equivalent property.

delay.description: How long to wait for the previous execution before starting another.

max_executions.description: How many *extra* executions a request may have.

TargetSchema.description: The target side of the schema (`CFG-130`).

keyspace_table.description: The target table, as `keyspace.table`. Defaults to the origin table (`CFG-023`).

cipher_suites.description: Cipher suites offered during the handshake.

enabled.description:
Whether to use TLS.

When enabled and no secure-connect-bundle is configured, the trust store, key
store and cipher suites must all be supplied (`CFG-025`).

is_astra.description: Whether this side is Astra, which implies its own trust material.

keystore.description: The client certificate this side presents.

truststore.description: The certificates this side will trust.

TokenBound.description: A partitioner token, as a decimal string. Murmur3 tokens span -2^63..2^63-1; RandomPartitioner tokens span 0..2^127.

TokenFilter.description: The slice of the token ring to process (`CFG-180`).

max.description: Highest token to process. Defaults to the partitioner's maximum.

min.description: Lowest token to process. Defaults to the partitioner's minimum.

auto_rerun.description: Automatically rerun the ranges the previous run did not complete.

enabled.description: Record each token range's outcome so the run can be resumed.

previous_run_id.description: The run to resume. `0` starts from the beginning.

rerun_multiplier.description: How many times to subdivide a range that is rerun.

run_id.description: The identifier to record this run under. `0` allocates a new one.

Transform.description: Changes applied to values on their way to the target (`CFG-170`).

codec_timestamp_format.description:
The `java.time` pattern the `TIMESTAMP_STRING_FORMAT` codec parses and prints.

Canonically `transform.codec_timestamp_format`. `docs/SPEC.md` §3.5.8 names this
`transform.codecs.timestamp_format`, which cannot coexist with the
`transform.codecs` list in a struct tree; the legacy alias is unaffected.

codec_timestamp_zone.description:
The IANA time zone the `TIMESTAMP_STRING_FORMAT` codec assumes.

Canonically `transform.codec_timestamp_zone`, for the reason given on
[`codec_timestamp_format`](Transform::codec_timestamp_format).

custom_ttl.description: TTL, in seconds, to use instead of the origin's. `0` disables.

custom_writetime.description: Writetime, in microseconds, to use instead of the origin's. `0` disables.

map_remove_null_value.description: Drop map entries whose value is null instead of writing them.

missing_key_ts_replace.description:
Timestamp, in epoch milliseconds, substituted for a null key column.

Partition and clustering columns cannot be null; when a schema change introduces
a key column the origin does not have, this supplies a constant in its place.

TrustStore.description: The trust store of one side (`CFG-120`).

TrustStoreType.description: The on-disk format of a trust store (`CFG-120`).

oneOf.description: A Java key store.
A PKCS#12 store.
PEM-encoded certificates.

automatic.description:
Use every eligible non-key column as a TTL source.

Naming columns explicitly disables this (`CFG-037`).

names.description: The columns whose TTL to read, largest wins.

TtlWritetime.description: How TTL and writetime are calculated (`CFG-130`).

use_collections.description:
Allow collection columns to contribute TTL and writetime.

Necessary when every non-key column is a collection, since Cassandra reports no
row-level TTL or writetime in that case.

automatic.description:
Use every eligible non-key column as a writetime source.

Naming columns explicitly disables this (`CFG-037`).

names.description: The columns whose writetime to read, largest wins.

max.description: Skip rows whose writetime is above this, in microseconds.

min.description: Skip rows whose writetime is below this, in microseconds.

description:
The complete configuration of a cdm-rs run (`CFG-001`).

Construct one with [`ConfigLoader`](crate::ConfigLoader) rather than by hand: only the
loader applies the layered precedence of `CFG-010`, resolves secret indirection
(`CFG-012`) and reports the diagnostics of `CFG-021`.

autocorrect.description: What the validate job repairs when it finds a difference (`CFG-140`).

connect.description: How to reach the origin and target clusters (`CFG-100`).

filter.description: Which rows take part in the run (`CFG-180`).

schema.description: Which tables and columns take part in the run (`CFG-130`).

transform.description: Changes applied to values on their way to the target (`CFG-170`).
